newsitem.title: JAPAN: Recent history of world's worst oil spills.
newsitem.headline: Recent history of world's worst oil spills.

text.p: Following is a chronology of the world's worst oil spills in recent history.

5 Jan 93 - UNITED KINGDOM - Oil poured on to the coast of northern Scotland's Shetland Islands after the 89,000-tonne Liberian-registered Braer hit rocks in heavy seas. The tanker carried 84,500 tonnes of crude oil. A huge oil slick stretched 25 miles (40 km) up the coast.

21 Jan 93 - SINGAPORE/INDONESIA/MALAYSIA - The 255,312-tonne Singapore-registered tanker Maersk Navigator collided with the empty tanker Sanko Honour in the Andaman Sea en route from Oman to Japan. It was carrying a cargo of nearly two million barrels of oil. Its ruptured port side leaked burning oil and spread a slick up to 35 miles (56 km) long off Sumatra drifting towards India's Nicobar Islands.

11 Feb 93 - NETHERLANDS - Up to 30,000 seabirds were feared killed by a paraffin oil slick thought to have been discharged by a passing ship during the past two weeks. It was the worst oill spill off the Dutch coast in five years.

9 Mar 93 - GERMANY/POLAND - The wreck of the Jan Heweliusz, a Polish ferry which sank in the Baltic off Germany on January 14, began leaking oil. The ship was estimated to have up to 80 tonnes of fuel on board.

3 Jun 93 - BELGIUM/UNITED KINGDOM - Seven crewmen from a British tanker, the British Trent, burned to death in a blazing sea of petrol about 15 miles (24 km) off Ostend after a collision with a Panamanian bulk carrier in thick fog. Two other crewmen were missing presumed dead. Belgian environmental officials and the ship's owner, British Petroleum, played down pollution dangers. The tanker was loaded with 24,000 tonnes of petrol, which poured out of a hole in the port bow.

19 Aug 93 - FRANCE - An oil slick off the French Riviera after a collision between a nuclear submarine and a supertanker was brought under control with no danger to beaches. The collision on August 17 caused two spills, one off Fos-sur-Mer and one further out.

15 Oct 93 - GREECE - Oil leaked from the Greek tanker Iliad killed wildlife and destroyed fish farms in the bay of Pylos. A three-mile-long (4.8 km) oil slick was caused when the tanker ran aground off the island of Spaktiria on October 9.

7 Jan 94 - PUERTO RICO - The Morris J. Furhman, a barge carrying about 1.5 million gallons of fuel oil, went aground off the northern side of the capital city harbour. 750,000 gallons of heavy fuel oil had been spilled and had spread to cover a six-mile (9.6 km) stretch of shore. Conado Beach, the Conado lagoon and San Juan Bay were all polluted.

6 Mar 94 - THAILAND - About 105,670 gallons of diesel fuel spilled into the sea some four miles (6.4 km) off the eastern Sriracha coast after a chartered oil tanker and an unidentified cargo ship collided. The tanker, the Visahakit 5, was carrying about 1.06 million gallons of diesel and liquefied petroleum gas.

16 Mar 94 - TURKEY - A cleanup effort was begun to scoop patches of crude from the Bosphorus waterway and remove oil washed onto shore after a fiery collision on March 13 between the tanker Nassia and the freighter Shipbroker, both Cypriot-flagged. The accident, the worst in the Bosphorus in 15 years, killed 29 crewmen.

31 Mar 94 - UAE - 15,900 tonnes of crude oil leaked into the Arabian Sea after the Panamanian-flagged supertanker Seki spilled the crude 10 miles (16 km) off the UAE port of Fujairah, just outside the Gulf, when it collided with the UAE tanker Baynunah, which was in ballast. Oil reached the UAE coast (April 2) north of Khor Fakkan close to the Strait of Hormuz. (April 4)- the oil slick severely polluted several beaches and was threatening more than 25 miles (40 km) of coastline.

8 May 94 - VIETNAM - The 1,220-tonne Vietnamese Chanoco I, carrying 1,012 tonnes of fuel oil and a 10,000-tonne Taiwanese ship Unihumanity collided in the Long Tau river near Ho Chi Minh City. About 200 tonnes spilled into the river from the Vietnamese ship causing a 200-tonne oil slick which killed fish and other wildlife.

14 June 94 - INDIA - Indian authorities began siphoning off 700 tonnes of oil from the Sea Transporter, a 6,000-tonne Greek cargo ship which had been anchored off Aguada after it ran aground following a cyclone on June 5.

23 June 94 - SOUTH AFRICA - An oil slick washing ashore on Dassen Island threatened a colony of endangered Jackass penguins and polluted mainland beaches. It was confirmed on June 28 that the Apollo Sea, a Chinese bulk carrier that was believed to have sunk on June 20, shortly after leaving Saldanha Bay, was the source of Cape Town's worst oil pollution disaster.
11 August 94 - USA - The Columbus Iselin, a ship conducting oil spill research, ran aground in the Looe Key National Marine Sanctuary off the Florida Keys and was leaking fuel.

2 October 94 - PORTUGAL - A Panamanian registered tanker, Cercal, spilled about 2,000 tonnes of crude into the sea after striking a rock on its way into Leixoes harbour, in the northern city of Oporto. The oil badly polluted one beach near the entrance to Leixoes port and smaller quantities of oil came ashore on other parts of the coast near Oporto.

17 October 94 - CHINA - 1,000 metres of beaches and reefs at Dongshan, a resort area at Qinhuangdao in Hebei province were polluted by an oil spill blamed on the Huahai Number Two tanker, owned by the state-run Huahai Company of Beijing.
5 June 95 - SINGAPORE - About 100 tonnes of fuel oil leaked from a bunker fuel barge after it collided with the freighter Sun Pulse. The fuel oil had begun washing up on the island's east coast.

11 July 95 - AUSTRALIA - An ore carrier, the Iron Baron, ran aground on a reef in southern Australian waters, spilling more than 500 tonnes of fuel oil and causing a major pollution scare for the island state of Tasmania. Thousands of fairy penguins were fouled oil.

25 July 95 - SOUTH KOREA - Oil leaking from the 275,782 deadweight tonne Sea Prince, a burning tanker, off South Korea has formed a slick 20 miles (32 km) in diameter. The ship was loaded with 83,000 tonnes of crude oil. It is drifting towards the country's best known sea resort. 700 tonnes of fuel oil estimated to have been leaked.

15 Feb 96 - UNITED KINGDOM - The coastguard called a full environmental alert when the 147,000 deadweight tonne Liberian-registered Sea Empress with a crew of 28 Russians hit rocks near the port of Milford Haven, Wales. The tanker, operated by Acomarit, had been carrying 130,000 tonnes of light crude oil. On Feb 20 an estimated 40,000 tonnes of crude oil spilled -- a third of its cargo -- creating a four-mile (six km) oil slick.

27 May 96 - USA - A barge operated by Buffalo Marine Services Inc and loaded with about 210,000 gallons of fuel oil ruptured as it sailed through the Houston Ship Channel. About 4,200 gallons of oil spilled into Galveston Bay, causing a five-mile-long (eight km) oil slick.

7 Jan 97 - JAPAN - Coastal fishing villages in northwestern Japan braced for economic and environmental catastrophe as oil slicks from sunken Russian tanker Nakhodka coated beaches and threatened prized shellfish beds. The spill from the ruptured tanker, leaked 5,200 tonnes (36,400 barrels) of heavy fuel oil and was described as Japan's second-worst.

2 July 97 - JAPAN - A supertanker struck a shallow reef in Tokyo Bay, a famed fishing ground, leaking an estimated 13,400 tonnes of crude oil, producing what was believed to be Japan's worst ever oil spill.
